subject: Request: Short-lived diagnostic data carveout for production incident (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Sara Bell <sara.bell@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@acmehealth.com>, audit@cloudaudit.io
Date: 2027-08-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production anomaly - request for brief snapshot/hold

Hi Marissa,

We are seeing a repeatable generation failure in our production usage of Redwood's hosted inference for patient-summary workflows (region: eu-west). The error surfaces in a subset of requests and only when inputs contain nested JSON arrays. Our on-call has captured traces but they are insufficient to root cause.

Request: can Redwood perform a timeboxed carveout (capture of relevant logs, request/response payloads and model KV traces) for a 6-hour window starting now, stored under a customer-managed key in the EU region? We understand this is an exception to retention settings and are willing to sign any short-form authorization you need.

Priority: high — this affects nightly batch summaries and one customer SLA. Please advise who we should loop in from Redwood for security/privilege review and the fastest path to approval.

Thanks,
Sara Bell
Sr. SRE, Acme Health
[support ticket: AH-4523]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bell <sara.bell@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-03T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Production anomaly - request for brief snapshot/hold

Sara —

Thanks for the alert and clear ask. Im looping in Security (Rishi), Privacy/Legal (Laura) and Platform Eng (Neha) to scope the exception and prescribe guardrails.

Initial thoughts / items we need from Acme to expedite approval:
- Confirm the minimum time window you need (you suggested 6 hours) and exact earliest timestamp for capture.
- Provide the list of data types to be included (examples: request payloads, full responses, KV cache dumps, traces).
- Confirm whether any PHI-equivalent fields are present in the payloads and whether Acme can pre-redact.

From Redwood side well draft a short authorization that:
- Limits access to named Redwood engineers and security (timeboxed).
- Stores artifacts encrypted with an Acme-managed EU KMS key.
- Auto-deletes artifacts after an agreed retention period (suggest 14 days) unless a follow-up escalation is opened.
- Records every access in an audit log and provides a signed manifest.

Rishi/Laura/Neha — can you review and propose the minimum controls and signoff timeline? I can pull the SLA exemption form and a manifest template and send to Sara for signature once we have agreement.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_exemption_form.pdf (stub)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-03T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production anomaly - request for brief snapshot/hold

Marissa / team —

Security assessment (preliminary):
- Acceptable with conditions. The key requirements Id insist on:
  - Artifacts must be encrypted with an Acme-provided EU KMS key (we will not retain plaintext copies outside of ephemeral worker memory).
  - Access must be limited to named Redwood engineers + a single security reviewer; no contractor access without explicit approval.
  - A strict chain-of-custody manifest must be produced (who accessed what and when).
  - Storage location: EU only (eu-west region).
- Recommended retention: 14 days auto-delete; if Acme requests an extension a formal escalation to Security+Legal is required.
- We should require Acme to indicate whether any payloads contain PHI-like fields; if present, require that Acme pre-redact or provide an equivalently scoped BAA amendment.

Ill prepare a short playbook (attached) for the engineers to follow during collection and a checklist for redaction/manifest entries. This will speed approvals.

-Rishi
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_temporary_access_playbook.pdf (stub)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sara Bell <sara.bell@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T11:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Production anomaly - request for brief snapshot/hold

Hi all —

Legal/Privacy position: we can approve a narrowly-scoped, timeboxed carveout with the following requirements before any data is captured:
1) Signed short-form authorization (Ive pre-filled the SLA_exemption_form.pdf that Marissa attached); signature can be via DocuSign (link below).
2) Explicit inventory of data types to be collected (Acme to provide).
3) Confirmation that Acme will either pre-redact direct patient identifiers or grant Redwood permission to apply redaction tooling prior to any engineer access.
4) Artifacts must be encrypted under Acme-managed EU KMS and access keys rotated after deletion.
5) Final retention window: 14 calendar days from collection end time; automatic deletion thereafter.
6) If any PHI or regulated identifiers are present, Acme must confirm BAA scope covers this collection or sign an addendum.

Once we have the signed form and the data inventory I (or a delegate) will sign off within 2 hours. Ive added a DocuSign link to the pre-filled form here: https://docusign.example.com/AcmeHealth-Triage-Form

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bell <sara.bell@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, audit@cloudaudit.io
Date: 2027-08-03T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production anomaly - request for brief snapshot/hold — plan and next steps

Sara —

Thanks for the quick responses. Below is the agreed plan so we have a single source of truth:

1) Collection window: 2027-08-03T09:00:00Z to 2027-08-03T15:00:00Z (Acme confirmed 6-hour window).
2) Data types to capture: request payloads (raw), model responses (raw), select KV cache traces filtered by session ID (Acme provided list), system traces.
3) PHI confirmation: Acme confirms there may be patient identifiers; Acme will pre-redact direct identifiers where feasible and has started the DocuSign for the BAA amendment.
4) Storage & encryption: artifacts stored in eu-west, encrypted with Acme KMS key supplied via KMS ARN; Redwood will only hold encrypted objects.
5) Access: limited to 3 named Redwood engineers (Neha, one backend eng TBD, and a security reviewer Rishi). All accesses will be recorded.
6) Retention: automatic deletion 14 days after collection end (2027-08-17T15:00:00Z) unless Acme submits a written extension request.
7) Deliverables: snapshot_manifest.json (contains checksums and access log entries) and a signed custody manifest after collection.

Action items for Acme:
- Sign the short-form authorization here: https://docusign.example.com/AcmeHealth-Triage-Form
- Send the session IDs for the affected requests and confirm whether pre-redaction is possible (reply to this thread).

Once we have the signed form and session IDs well kick off collection and share a read-only manifest link.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: snapshot_manifest.json (stub)
From: DevOps Team <devops@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Bell <sara.bell@acmehealth.com>, audit@cloudaudit.io
Date: 2027-08-03T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Production anomaly - request for brief snapshot/hold — plan and next steps

Marissa —

Thanks, confirmed and DocuSigned. Session IDs: sess-AC-1203, sess-AC-1209, sess-AC-1212. We will redact direct patient IDs for sess-AC-1212 (contains PHI) and leave the other two as-is for fidelity.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please proceed with the collection under the conditions above.

—Acme DevOps
